title: I Took the Salon No-Show Fee Straight to the Owner's Sister

parts.text: I arrived at 10:00 a.m. with wet hair from the rain and a confirmation text that said WE'RE READY. The receptionist did not look up. "Lena isn't here. You didn't confirm yesterday." I showed her the thread: I had confirmed at 7:12 p.m. She shrugged. "Policy is a fifty-dollar no-show if we don't see the text." I was twenty-six, paying with a paycheck that still smelled like printer toner. Lena was the owner's sister. She walked in at 10:19 eating a bagel, saw me, and said, "Oh, I thought you cancelled." I asked for the policy sheet. It said no-show fees apply when the client fails to confirm. I had confirmed. They still charged my card fifty dollars while I sat under a dripping umbrella. I screenshotted the charge, the texts, and the policy. Then Lena's next client sat in my chair. I smiled at the camera behind the register because I had just noticed it faced the desk, not the chairs.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They charged me for a no-show while I stood there; the camera saw the desk.

social.video_title: They billed me while I waited in the rain — Part 1/2
social.description: Confirmed appointment, fifty-dollar no-show, and the owner's sister eating a bagel in my slot. The register camera was watching the desk. Would you have walked out?

parts.text: I emailed the owner with three attachments and the timestamp from the register camera request form on the wall. "Client present, stylist late, fee applied in reverse," I wrote. The owner called at 2:04. She said Lena had been having a hard week. I said my card had a hard fifty dollars. They reversed the fee and offered a free blowout. I took the reversal and declined the blowout. I posted a review that only quoted the policy sheet and the confirmation text. Lena commented that I was dramatic. I replied with the camera request form number. The salon updated the policy: no-show fees cannot be charged if the client is physically in the lobby. I get my hair cut two blocks over now. The umbrella dried. The fifty dollars came back on a Thursday.

social.video_title: The register camera disagreed with the bagel — Part 2/2
social.description: Policy sheet, confirmation text, and a fee charged in reverse. They updated the rule after the camera request. Was a bagel ever a cancellation?
